breakEven.model: net_savings_ms = verifier_execution_ms (control child-process time of the avoided verifiers) - reuse_check_ms (treatment wall - control non-verifier wall, measured per pair). Break-even verifier cost ~= reuse_check_ms. Linearity is checked, not assumed (see residuals).

rationale: Reuse is net-negative below ~152.4 ms of verifier cost and consistently net-positive for expensive verifiers; a cost gate at the measured threshold captures the benefit without the cheap-verifier loss.

historicalCostEstimation.where: VerificationEvidence.elapsedMs (ForgeVerify child-process wall time), persisted verbatim inside the 'evidence' work-item payload by createForgeVerifyPersistenceObserver and returned by loadForgeVerifyEvidence; also surfaced as VerifierRunResult.durationMs and VerificationReceipt.durationMs.
historicalCostEstimation.separationNote: Duration must only ever inform a ForgeGreen cost policy (e.g. a future gate deciding whether to spend reuse_check_ms at all). It never participates in validity: ForgeVerify's isEvidenceCurrentlyValid remains the sole authority and takes no duration input.
